subject: Onboarding & Index Migration: Vector Search + Rerank Plan
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Liu <emma@docuverse.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Onboarding & Index Migration: Vector Search + Rerank Plan

Hi Emma —

Great to meet you on the call earlier. Per our conversation, I’m kicking off the formal handoff from Sales to CS/Implementation and summarizing a proposed plan for the vector-search + rerank migration. High-level asks below; I’ve attached a short checklist and a SOW draft for review.

Summary goals
- Replace current in-house vector index with a Redwood-backed flow (choice of managed vector DB or self-hosted per compliance)
- Implement a reranker step for top-K results to improve relevance (target +10-15% MRR uplift on query tests)
- Migrate existing index with minimal downtime and a staged canary rollout

Proposed timeline
- Kickoff / alignment call: this week — 60 min
- Access & export validation: 1 week
- Index backfill (incremental): 2–3 weeks depending on dataset size
- Rerank evals + tuning: 1 week
- Canary rollout + monitoring window: 2 weeks

Immediate asks for kickoff
1) Provide a 1–2 GB sample export or a representative JSONL (fields: id, text, metadata) — helps define embedding pipeline.
2) Confirm expected document counts and average doc size (approx rows & chars).
3) Share who will be the engineering owner(s) on your side (for access, keys).

Technical notes / options (brief)
- Vector DB options we commonly recommend: Pinecone (SaaS, simple), Milvus/Weaviate (self-hosted), RedisVector (if you need a hybrid cache). Tradeoffs: Pinecone simpler; Milvus gives more control and is cheaper at scale in dedicated configs.
- Backfill approach: incremental partitioned workers, write-forward strategy with dual-read during canary. We can provide backfill scripts as part of onboarding.
- Rerank evals: we’ll run an NDCG@10 and MRR baseline, plus manual relevance checks on ~500 queries in the first pass.

Attachments: redwood-onboard-checklist.pdf (checklist), draft-sow.docx (SOW), example export (if you can provide)

Next steps
- Emma: can you confirm an engineering contact + a sample export by EOD Monday?
- Monica: can you schedule an internal kickoff for Tuesday (CS + SE + Eng)?

Thanks — excited to get this moving.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Onboarding & Index Migration: Vector Search + Rerank Plan

Emma — thanks for the quick response and the sample export. I’ve reviewed the JSONL and the schema looks straightforward. I’ll own the CS coordination on Redwood’s side.

A few practical notes for the kickoff and access:
- Access: we’ll need a scoped S3 read role (or secure upload link) for the full export. If you prefer private deployment, we’ll route this through the Private onboarding playbook and involve Security.
- Backfill estimate: rough ballpark for 12M docs with average 1.1k chars — assuming 256-dim embeddings and standard batching, incremental backfill with 8 parallel workers should complete in ~10–14 days. Final estimate after we validate export and confirm embedding throughput.
- Vector DB recommendation: if you need Private + control, Milvus or Weaviate in your VPC is a good fit. If you want fastest time-to-value with managed ops, Pinecone is simplest. We can produce cost/latency comparisons in Kickoff.

Rerank evaluation plan (high level)
- Create a test set: 500 queries (mix of high/low traffic + head/tail intent)
- Baselines: current retrieval (BM25 or existing vector) and post-rerank score
- Metrics: MRR, NDCG@10, top1 accuracy (manual labels on 100 queries)
- Acceptance criteria: +8–12% lift in MRR or matched to product KPIs (we’ll align with you)

I attached a starter rerank-eval-matrix.csv to collect sample queries and labels during the kickoff.

Monica
Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>, Emma Liu <emma@docuverse.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onboarding & Index Migration: Vector Search + Rerank Plan

Emma / team — I did a quick technical pass on the export and the migration constraints. A few practical implementation items and recommendations: 

Index backfill plan (detailed)
- Approach: incremental, partition-by-range (doc_id hash) with idempotent workers. Write strategy: we recommend write-forward into a new index while keeping the current index available for reads. During canary, route X% of traffic to new index + reranker.
- Backfill throughput knobs: recommended batch size 512, tokenization and embedding compute parallelized across 16 GPUs (or equivalent CPU+GPU workers).
- Estimated throughput: ~80–120k docs/day per 16-GPU cluster (varies by model & token length). For 12M docs, estimate 10–16 days depending on concurrency — aligns with Monica’s ballpark.
- Storage: expect ~1.4x raw size for indexes with metadata and quantized vectors; plan capacity accordingly.

Rerank and evals
- Reranker model should be warmed on the test set; we recommend holding out a validation set for quick iteration.
- Metric tracking: set up dashboards for MRR, NDCG@10, p95 latency, and error rate. Tie alerts to p95 > 250ms or error rate > 1%.

Fallback strategy
- Canary: 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% over 48–72 hour windows with performance gates. Automated rollback to prior index if MRR drops >5% or p95 latency increases >30%.

I’ve attached a draft SOW with scope and milestones (draft-sow.docx). Happy to refine during kickoff.

Laura Bennett
Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Onboarding & Index Migration: Vector Search + Rerank Plan

Thanks all — couple of operational points to lock in: 
- Canary schedule: propose we begin with a 5% traffic canary for 48 hours, validate metrics, then move to 25% for 72 hours. If green, proceed to 100% over a week.
- Monitoring: I’ll instrument the routes with token-level tracing and cost breakdowns so product can observe unit economics during ramp.
- Rerank eval dataset: Emma — can you confirm whether the 500 queries should be sampled from production logs or curated? If production, we’ll need an anonymized query dump.
- Access: please share an S3 read role or an SFTP account for the full export. We’ll request minimum permissions.

Small ask: Monica — can you own the runbook for rollback (simple checklist + who to page)? I’ll add automatic fallback hooks in the routing policy.

Thanks — Karthik
Applied ML / Infra
Redwood Inference
